lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice using present perfect for recent updates that matter now.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Two colleagues compare what they have already done before or during a workday.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Giving short status updates and asking whether something is done.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik talk during a break about lunch, errands, and small tasks they have already done or not done yet.

main_focus.name: present perfect for recent updates
main_focus.description: Use har plus supine to describe completed actions with present relevance.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use present perfect naturally 4-5 times in the dialogue.

avoid_grammar: detailed preterite storytelling as the main focus

useful_chunks: Vad skönt att det är klart.
vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use time adverbs with present perfect when they sound natural.

dialogue_shape.opening: One person asks whether a small task or meal is already done.
dialogue_shape.middle: They compare two or three recent actions using present perfect.
dialogue_shape.ending: They decide what still needs to happen next.

target_complexity.repetition: several natural har plus supine examples are desired

focus: which tasks or activities are already done
which task or activity is not done yet
what still needs to happen next

sentence_focus: one sentence with har inte än
one question with Har du hunnit
one sentence about a recent meal or errand
one sentence saying what still needs to be done
